subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord plugin-owned self-profile action/API for bot-only nickname, avatar, status, and activity updates, and what gate, account-selection, validation, audit, and partial-failure contract should it use?
rationale: Current code lacks the requested surface, and implementation would create a new bot-credential-backed identity mutation path plus public config/action surface that automation should not choose without maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Approve narrow self-profile action
options.body: Add a default-off Discord `self-profile` action with strict self-only checks, explicit account selection, avatar validation, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Limit to presence-only work
options.body: Reject nickname/avatar mutation for now and route only the status/activity subset through the existing presence action or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/29725.

options.title: Defer identity mutation
options.body: Keep bot identity changes manual or external until maintainers define a broader Discord identity model across self-profile, per-binding identity, and webhooks.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-profile action
recommendation.body: Add a default-off Discord `self-profile` action with strict self-only checks, explicit account selection, avatar validation, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord presence-health work and the PR discussion that left self-profile out of scope.
